task_language: put the right moka pot on the stove

subtasks.name: pick(right_moka_pot)
subtasks.outcome: failed: picked the other pot. The robot's right pot is the image-left one; pi0 grasped the image-centre pot (robot's left, nearest the stove)

subtasks.name: place(right_moka_pot, stove, on)
subtasks.outcome: never attempted with the correct pot; the wrong pot was placed and then toppled onto its side (step 300-320)

behaviour_summary: pi0 picks the pot nearest the stove (the same first pot it takes in libero_10 'put both moka pots on the stove'), sets it on the stove tilted, the pot topples on release, pi0 comes back and presses on it (340-380) and leaves it lying on the stove.
runs_trained_task: libero_10 KITCHEN_SCENE8: put both moka pots on the stove (first-pot phase)

failures.mode_definition: The policy selects a same-category object other than the one identified by a spatial qualifier (left/right/front/back) in the instruction.
hl_remedy: if the wrong pot is on the stove: INSERT_SUBTASK "pick up the left moka pot and place it on the table"
REPROMPT "put the right moka pot on the stove"
WATCH 5 s for an approach to the image-left (robot's right) pot
failures.prevention: Coordinator grounds the qualifier to one instance (image-left = robot's right) before running pi0, and the FR agent HALTs when the EE descends on the non-target instance.
failures.observation: At step 60 the gripper is above the table between the pots; by 80-120 it descends onto the image-centre pot (the robot's left pot) and lifts it at 180-200. The image-left pot never moves.

failures.mode_definition: The object is set down tilted or off-centre and topples on release, ending on its side instead of upright on the destination.
failures.rl_success_check: moka pot upright on the stove cook region, gripper open and clear
failures.observation: At 260-280 the pot is held over the stove; at 300 it is tilted as the gripper opens; at 320 it lies on its side across the burner. Steps 340-380 pi0 comes back down on top of it without righting it; at 409 it is still on its side.

notes: Left/right follows the protocol convention (robot's left = image right). If the BDDL 'right' pot were the image-centre one, the primary failure would instead be the LL tip-over; the tip-over alone would fail the task in either case. I could not check init0 to compare.
